answer: Each peer’s EigenTrust contribution decays exponentially with a defined half-life, so reputation requires sustained honest service to remain influential. Reciprocity-weighted transitivity and matrix-factorized trust build centrality from corroborated links; a freshly spawned sybil has almost no trusted incoming paths, leaving its eigenvector centrality near zero and unable to pass consensus. Like a reef in the ocean, trust grows gradually, with each pulse of verified service strengthening it.
